## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single anonymous: authors do not learn the identity of reviewers or the associate editor unless they choose to reveal it; reviewers know the authors' identities. Sources: https://aij.ijcai.org/confidentiality-and-anonymity/ and https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/ (both retrieved 2026-11-23; page footers show a date of 04 July 2021, so the wording may be older than the live practice) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Yes, offered by the publisher: the archived guide (2024-03-27) says an editor may suggest transfer to another journal through the Elsevier Article Transfer Service, and the manuscript is then reviewed independently by the new journal (https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Neither the archived guide nor the journal's reviewing pages mention publication of reports |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | The archived guide says that, except in extenuating circumstances, only one revision of a submitted manuscript is considered. The journal's reviewing page says an article can normally not get "major revision" more than once, and that a minor revision is usually checked by the associate editor, though a second review by selected reviewers is not uncommon (https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/; retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | The first stage can end in rejection, acceptance, or a major or minor revision invitation. The policy is three reviews usually, two in special circumstances, with the first outcome decided by the associate editor (https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/; retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific text beyond the Elsevier house policy, which the live guide for authors (read 2026-11-23, section "Declaration of generative AI use") and the archived guide (2024-03-27) reproduce |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. Use is allowed with a mandatory disclosure statement |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as the Mind entry). The 2024 archived guide limited use to improving readability and language; the live guide (2026-11-23) no longer carries that limit and lets authors use AI tools with human oversight and a declaration (see Summary) |
| **Summary** | Live guide for authors (read 2026-11-23): authors may use AI tools to support them, never as a substitute for human critical thinking, and only under human oversight and control; use must be declared upon submission in a statement placed in a new section before the reference list, which appears in the published work; the declaration does not apply to basic tools that check grammar, spelling and references or to disability-related assistive technology used solely for accessibility; AI tools may not be listed or cited as author; the journal does not allow editors and reviewers to upload an unpublished manuscript into a generative AI tool. The 2024 wording "only to improve readability and language" is not in the live text. Older copy, archived guide (2024-03-27): generative AI and AI-assisted tools should be used only to improve readability and language, with human oversight; AI cannot be listed or cited as an author; authors add a statement before the reference list naming the tool and reason, and the statement appears in the published work; basic grammar and spelling checks need no disclosure. Elsevier's publisher page (retrieved 2026-11-23, read through a summarising fetch tool, not the raw page): authors may also use AI to synthesise literature or organise content with verification, must not use generative AI to create or alter images except as part of a described method, and reviewers and editors may not upload manuscripts to generative AI tools. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors (live, 2026-11-23); older copy https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors and https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/the-use-of-generative-ai-and-ai-assisted-technologies-in-writing-for-elsevier |

### Preprint Policy

> Source: live guide for authors (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors, read 2026-11-23), the archived guide for authors (2024-03-27, https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors) and Elsevier's sharing page (https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/sharing; retrieved 2026-11-23, read through a summarising fetch tool). The accepted-manuscript embargo for this journal is listed by Elsevier in a per-journal spreadsheet that was not read.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The live guide (2026-11-23) says preprints may be shared in line with Elsevier's article sharing policy and that sharing on a preprint server will not count as prior publication; the 2024 copy said preprints can be shared anywhere at any time |
| Under review | Yes | Same sentences as above (the live guide states no restriction during review; the 2024 copy said "anywhere at any time"); the journal's reviewing pages say reviewers know author identities, so a public preprint costs no anonymity |

| Version of Record | Open access articles per their licence; subscription-route articles are not for public repositories | Per Elsevier's sharing page |

## Format

> Source for the general rules: the journal's own editorial site (https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/, https://aij.ijcai.org/formatting-requirements/, https://aij.ijcai.org/call-for-papers/; retrieved 2026-11-23) and the live guide for authors (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors, read 2026-11-23) with the archived guide for authors (https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors, copy dated 2024-03-27) for details the live read did not re-check.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Regular papers, Research Notes, Research Field Reviews and position papers ("Turing Tape" papers; both by invitation, after a two-page proposal), book reviews, and competition summary papers (archived guide). OpenAlex type counts, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 540 articles, 60 paratext, 5 errata, 4 editorials, 2 conference abstracts, 1 book review (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | No page limit for regular papers (https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/); the journal advises twenty to thirty A4 or Letter pages in 11 pt single column, and the archived guide warns that papers over about forty pages are often significantly delayed. Research Notes: at most 4500 words, typically 5 to 14 pages |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Not applicable for regular papers (no limit stated); for Research Notes the 4500-word figure is worded as a maximum |
| **Abstract limit** | 250 words: the live guide (read 2026-11-23) says the abstract is concise, factual and "does not exceed 250 words", with 1 to 10 keywords in English. The 2024 archived guide gave no word count (older dated reading). Optional highlights: 3 to 5 bullet points of at most 85 characters each (live guide; same in the 2024 copy) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap stated. The archived guide sets a numbered list in alphabetical order by first author |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed and published as received (archived guide); the competition-paper section allows online appendices |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit stated; figures and tables should be embedded in the text for review (archived guide) |
| **Style / submission format** | English only, "grammatically correct" or the paper may be rejected without review; submit through Editorial Manager (https://www.editorialmanager.com/artint/default.aspx); single-column layout, at least 11 pt, no double-column conference format; keywords at most 10; elsarticle LaTeX class recommended; Unedited theses are acceptable only in exceptional circumstances. A conference version does not by itself disqualify a paper on novelty, though the guide says conference papers rarely meet the completeness criterion without extension |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a scope and contribution framing is stated by the journal itself: papers should articulate their relevance to artificial intelligence, clarify what is new, and include a motivational discussion; application papers should focus on how new AI methods advance performance rather than present another application of conventional methods (https://aij.ijcai.org/call-for-papers/ and the archived guide, copy dated 2024-03-27). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Papers must be "mature, complete, and novel" in the guide's wording, include relevant proofs or experimental data, and discuss connections to existing literature; heavily mathematical papers should include a less technical introduction for a broad readership, and papers that are purely mathematical without demonstrated applicability to AI may be returned (archived guide, https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors).
- **Article types**: regular papers; Research Notes of at most 4500 words; invited Research Field Reviews and position papers after a two-page proposal; book reviews; competition summary papers that must say why the competition matters beyond its own series (archived guide and https://aij.ijcai.org/call-for-papers/).
- **Prior publication**: a conference version by the same authors does not disqualify on novelty, but the journal says conference papers rarely meet its completeness criterion without extension (https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/; retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the journal's reviewing page says it is common for articles to be rejected without review by the editor-in-chief or an associate editor when too weak or out of scope (https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/; retrieved 2026-11-23); the submission page says papers not in correct English may be rejected without review.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex works API, 612 records; 255 with an abstract, of which 253 are hybrid open-access records, so these shares describe the open-access subset). Shares use the 255 records with an abstract as denominator; each pattern is a case-insensitive Python regular expression over title plus abstract, named in backticks and listed exactly in "Exact keyword patterns" (AI-Research Notes). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Counts are lower bounds. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `experiment` 52 of 255 (20.4%); `empirical` 30 (11.8%); `benchmark` 33 (12.9%). The journal asks for demonstrations of value and effectiveness (https://aij.ijcai.org/call-for-papers/) |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | `interview` zero of 255. Human-subject studies of other kinds: of 10 matches for `user_study_participants`, 7 describe human-subject studies on manual reading (for example https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2025.104282, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2026.104621), so 7 of 255 = 2.7% |
| Autoethnography | 0 | `autoethnography` zero of 255 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `theorem_proof_complexity` 37 of 255 (14.5%). The guide asks for all relevant proofs and experimental data (archived guide, 2024-03-27). `philosophical` matches 1 of 255 (0.4%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | `mixed_methods` zero of 255 |
| Meta-analysis | 0 | `meta_analysis` zero of 255. Reviews do appear: `survey_review` 5 of 255 (2.0%); the journal runs invited Research Field Reviews (archived guide) |

Among the 12 newest abstracts (2026-09-26 to 2026-11-14; `we_our` on the abstract alone), 9 match, for example https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2026.104657 and https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2026.104661; three do not, including https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2026.104660 and https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2026.104644. These are abstracts, not article introductions; the archived guide gives no rule on first person. Single-author articles: 20 of 540 (3.7%) in OpenAlex |
| **Expected density** | No page limit; the journal advises twenty to thirty single-column 11 pt pages (https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/). Heavily mathematical papers should add a high-level introduction accessible to a wide audience and explanatory commentary throughout (archived guide, 2024-03-27) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Concise, factual, self-contained abstract of at most 250 words; 1 to 10 keywords; optional highlights of 3 to 5 bullets of at most 85 characters (live guide, read 2026-11-23; the 2024 copy stated no abstract word count and at most 10 keywords) |
| **Writing style notes** | English only, American or British usage but not mixed (archived guide); numbered sections 1, 1.1, 1.1.1; references numbered and listed alphabetically by first author; unedited theses accepted only in exceptional circumstances; the guide's generic section list (introduction, material and methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is publisher template text, and the sampled abstracts show formal, theory-and-experiment papers (see Methodological Preferences); full article structure was not sampled |
| **Authorship pattern** | Single-author articles 20 of 540 (3.7%); Crossref author lists: 25 single-author of 661 records that list authors (3.8%) (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0004-3702/works; retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | The live board page (2026-11-23) lists 62 associate editors and 80 editorial board members (148 entries including editors-in-chief, field review editors, a competition editor and an awards track editor); the archived board page (copy 2024-04-27) listed 62 associate editors and 101 editorial board members (168 entries). The archived page's listed specialties cover knowledge representation, reasoning, planning, multi-agent systems, machine learning, natural language processing and social choice; countries are counted in Epistemological & Political Leanings (the 148 live entries sum by country to 148; the 168 archived entries sum to 168). The journal says submissions are reviewed partly by editorial board members and partly by other qualified researchers | https://web.archive.org/web/20240427113602/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/about/editorial-board ; https://aij.ijcai.org/faq-for-prospective-reviewers/ ; retrieved 2026-11-23; board composition may have changed since |
| **Reviewer list size** | Not published as a list; the journal's policy is three reviews usually and two in special circumstances per paper (https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/) | Journal reviewing page, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Review model** | Single anonymous: authors do not know reviewers' identities; reviewers know the authors; reviewers normally see the other reviews after returning their own (https://aij.ijcai.org/confidentiality-and-anonymity/) | Journal confidentiality page, retrieved 2026-11-23; footer date 04 July 2021 |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report exists beyond 2 SciRev reviews with no ratings shown (https://scirev.org/journal/artificial-intelligence/); LetPub's 37 user reviews were not read (https://www.letpub.com/journal-selector/journal/892) | Recorded gap |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. Qualitative-interview methods match zero of 255 abstracts, which shows the method is absent from the sample, not how reviewers would treat it | OpenAlex counts, see Methodological Preferences |
| **Discourse community signals (author side)** | Author community as a proxy, not a reviewer list: China 137, United States 119, United Kingdom 113, Italy 86, Germany 57 works with at least one author there (OpenAlex, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23). Board counts, live page 2026-11-23: China 22, United States 20, United Kingdom 19, Italy 14, Australia 9 and France 9 of 148 entries; older archived copy (2024-04-27): United States 22, China 19, United Kingdom 18, Italy 15, France 12 of 168 entries | OpenAlex works API, the live board page and the archived board page, retrieved 2026-11-23 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No journal-specific ethics-approval rule on the pages read; the archived guide (2024-03-27) points to Elsevier's general ethics-in-publishing information and asks for sex- and gender-based reporting for research involving humans (https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors). Human-subject studies appear in 7 of 255 abstracts (Methodological Preferences) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author articles are 20 of 540 (3.7%) in OpenAlex for 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23, and 25 of 661 (3.8%) in Crossref author lists |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The archived guide asks for the affiliation where the work was done and states no rule on unaffiliated authors; no count of unaffiliated authors was made |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The archived guide says the journal "requires and enables you to share data" supporting a publication where appropriate, including software, code, models and algorithms, and asks that data be cited in the reference list (https://web.archive.org/web/20240327100337/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/artificial-intelligence/publish/guide-for-authors) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Review is single anonymous: reviewers know author identities (https://aij.ijcai.org/confidentiality-and-anonymity/); preprints are allowed anywhere at any time (archived guide). the corresponding author must supply CRediT contributor roles for the co-authors (archived guide) |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement before the reference list; AI may not be an author (archived guide, 2024-03-27, and the Elsevier page, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; no fee on the subscription route; APC USD 3,650 excluding taxes on the live journal home (2026-11-23; USD 4,050 in the 2026-03-21 snapshot). IJCAI affiliates can read the journal free of charge through a separate agreement (https://aij.ijcai.org/free-access-to-the-ai-journal/) |
| **Originality and length** | Results must not have been published by others or by the same authors in an archival journal; unedited theses only in exceptional circumstances (https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/; archived guide) |

**Method note:** OpenAlex was used sparingly (7 direct requests: sources lookup, 2 count requests, 4 paged downloads of up to 200 records, plus the import script's own) without any key or email and without HTTP 429. Keyword shares were counted locally from the downloaded records, so every share has an exact pattern. Board countries were counted from the archived page's HTML, one entry per editor; one entry lists two affiliations and was counted under the first. Shares of the 255 abstracts come from article records that are almost all hybrid open-access, and "participants" or "qualitative" matches were read by hand where the text says so.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Novelty and completeness**: the guide requires results not previously published by others or by the same authors in an archival journal, and says conference papers rarely meet the completeness criterion without extension (Framing Requirements; https://aij.ijcai.org/submitting-an-article/).
- **Scope**: purely mathematical work without demonstrated applicability to AI may be returned (Framing Requirements; archived guide, 2024-03-27); papers outside scope are commonly rejected without review (https://aij.ijcai.org/about-reviewing/).
- **Language**: papers not in grammatically correct English may be rejected without review (Format).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use in writing breaches the stated policy (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval rules and the embargo length are unknown (Practical Concerns blanks), and the guide copy is from 2024.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher displays about 389 days from submission to acceptance (Review Cycle Time; display figure, definition not given), and the journal's own page gives about 20 weeks to a first decision for papers sent to review.
- **Length**: no limit, but the journal advises 20 to 30 pages and warns that papers over about forty pages are often significantly delayed (Format).
- **Open access cost**: gold open access carries a USD 3,650 APC on the live journal home of 2026-11-23 (USD 4,050 in the 2026-03-21 snapshot) (Open Access); green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to a journal-specific embargo that was not read (Preprint Policy).
- **Anonymity**: review is single anonymous, so reviewers see author identities (Peer Review).

### Best Suited For

- Formal, algorithmic or empirical AI work with proofs or demonstrated results: `experiment` 20.4%, `theorem_proof_complexity` 14.5% of 255 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Work in knowledge representation, planning, constraint solving, argumentation, multi-agent systems, social choice and reinforcement learning, each 7.5% to 9.8% of abstracts (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Teams of several authors: single-author articles are 20 of 540 (Voice & Style).
- Authors with a conference version that has been substantially extended (Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- Qualitative, interview-based, ethnographic or mixed-methods studies: zero of 255 abstracts match the corresponding patterns (Methodological Preferences). This shows absence from the sample, not rejection.
- Authors needing a verified fast turnaround: the only figures are publisher displays without definitions and a policy page whose footer dates from 2021 (Review Cycle Time).
- Work whose main contribution is philosophical, sociological or policy analysis of AI: `philosophical` matches 1 of 255 abstracts and `ethics` 3 of 255 (Methodological Preferences, Sensitive Topics), although "ethical AI" is named in the aims.

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that exist in this corpus or are named in the journal's own materials, listed only because they share the subject area; they are not a claim about acceptance odds. The publisher's article transfer service can also propose a transfer within Elsevier (Peer Review).

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research](journal-of-artificial-intelligence-research.md) | Same subject area (general AI); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [Nature Machine Intelligence](nature-machine-intelligence.md) | Same broad subject area; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [ACM Transactions on Interactive Intelligent Systems](../psychology/acm-transactions-on-interactive-intelligent-systems.md) | Closer to human-facing AI, which is a small share of this journal's abstracts (`human_ai_interaction` 1.6%); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
